But C is at row7-9, not row2. So A can slide to col0? It occupies cols0-3 row2. Since no overlap with C, yes leftmost 0. But wait is there any rule that preserves relative horizontal order between objects? In examples, objects are packed left in order, but if no vertical overlap, they can share columns. Example3: color1 at c2 and color2 at c4, disjoint rows, both moved to c0. So yes A can go to c0.

Then B: original at c5-6 rows6-9. Occupies rows6-9. C occupies rows7-9 cols0-2. B must avoid C. Also A row2 no overlap. So B can slide left until its leftmost column?
